name: Iowa

windshield.strip: No strip/AS-1 exception stated; windshield must meet 70% light transmittance

frontSide.note: side window to the immediate right or left of the driver and front sidewings

backSide.note: no transparency standard; only general 'clear vision' rule of § 321.438(1)

rear.note: no transparency standard; only general 'clear vision' rule of § 321.438(1)

tint.measuredHow: not stated (rule says the windshield/window must meet 70 percent light transmittance)

reflectivity.front: may not be 'excessively dark or reflective' (no numeric limit)

medicalExemption.text: No medical exemption for new tint. Vehicles with a dark window exemption issued before July 4, 2012 remain under former rule 761-450.7(3) as in effect April 13, 2022.

tint.lastAmended: Statute: 2021 Acts ch 183 §53; rule renumbered 450.5 by ARC 9133C, effective 2025-05-21
quotes: a front windshield, a side window to the immediate right or left of the driver, or a sidewing forward of and to the left or right of the driver which is excessively dark or reflective
"Excessively dark or reflective" means that the windshield, front side window or front sidewing does not meet a minimum standard of transparency of 70 percent light transmittance.
Motor vehicles operating with a dark window exemption issued prior to July 4, 2012, are subject to the provisions of rule 761—450.7(3) in effect April 13, 2022.

helmet.conditions: No motorcycle helmet requirement in Iowa Code § 321.275 (operation of motorcycles)

handheldPhone.fineText: $100 scheduled fine; warnings only until January 1, 2026 (hands-free law, 2025 Acts ch 14)

studdedTires.season: Nov 1 - Apr 1 (studs max 1/16 in.; school buses and fire apparatus any time)

radarDetector.note: No state ban on radar detectors in private passenger vehicles found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

underglow.rule: No red light visible from directly in front; flashing lights prohibited except listed uses; blue lights restricted to emergency vehicles (no specific underglow statute)

openQuestions: Iowa hands-free law (2025 Acts ch 14) is new: enforcement with citations began January 1, 2026 - confirm no further change.
Primary enforcement assumed (statute contains no secondary-enforcement clause).
Lift/frame height: no Iowa statute located.
